Grace / Marcus — assessment below (TL;DR at top). I also ran a quick sim against our east-us p95 on similar workloads and attached the spreadsheet (slo-impact-analysis.xlsx).

TL;DR: 120ms P95 is feasible for short-generation traffic only if we: provision a dedicated pool (4x A10G equiv), enable aggressive KV prefix caching, limit sequence length to 128 tokens for the SLA route, and add a warm standby pool for burst spikes. With those controls expected steady p95 ~90–110ms; under heavy bursts it could hit 140–160ms unless we add burst autoscale (adds cost).

Details:
- Baseline: For our current high-priority customers with similar mix (short prompts + facts retrieval) east-us p95 median ~110ms with dedicated 3x A10G pool and prefix caching enabled.
- Traffic mix assumptions: Mosaic indicated 80% short-generation (<128 tokens), 15% function-calls, 5% long-chat (we asked for confirmation). If long-chat is >10% we cannot commit to 120ms P95 without model variant downgrade or stricter rate-limits.
- Model/kernel choices: use a quantized 8-bit variant with attention optimizations; function-calling increases tail by ~30ms on average.
- Dedicated pool sizing: recommendation = 4x A10G (initial), hot standby 1x A10G for burst, configured with pre-warmed contexts and continuous batching window tuned to 5–10ms.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching expected to reduce token compute by ~25% for their distribution; must enable request-level cache keying and TTL policy.
- Rollback/triggers: breach = 2 p95 violations in a rolling 7-day window or single-day 4+ hour sustained p95 > 160ms; automated traffic split to backup model variant and notification to on-call.
- Observability: must add a per-route SLI dashboard, real-time alerts (PagerDuty) and a weekly quality regression check against the Mosaic prompt set.

Operational impacts & mitigations:
- Cost: estimated incremental monthly cost for dedicated pool + standby + added telemetry = ~$18k–25k depending on burst autoscale config. Marcus, confirm if Mosaic expects Redwood to absorb credits.
- Certification: Security/compliance team: no additional data residency constraints, standard SOC2 controls suffice.

Recommended approval path:
1) Product/Ops sign-off on config (this thread) — complete by EOD Wed (2027-06-23)
2) Finance review pricing/credits + legal redline (Marcus to share initial ask)
3) Exec approval (Aditya) for SLA exception and pricing adjustments
4) Onboard runbook + 2-week staging with Canary traffic, then GA cutover

I attached the impact spreadsheet and a short operations checklist in the sheet. Happy to walk through it at 11am PT if helpful.

—Monica
Principal Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
